format.name: agent-journal/events-jsonl
format.record_rule: a line whose top-level member 'declaration' is an object is a declaration record; every other line is an OCSF execution event carrying class_uid

1.caption: Canonical single observation
1.description: The only observation of its entity and stage among the declared sources.

2.caption: Supporting observation
2.description: One source's observation of an entity whose consolidated canonical event is in the same file.

3.caption: Consolidated canonical
3.description: The canonical event of an entity and stage that several sources observed, built from their compatible fields with per-field evidence.

2.caption: Representation only
2.description: Equal values spelled differently (1 and 1.0).

3.caption: One richer
3.description: One observation carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

4.caption: Each richer
4.description: Each carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

5.caption: Conflicting
5.description: Two observations report different values for one field.

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded
8.description: A provisional observation of a quantity that a final observation of the same quantity (same scope, aggregation and model) supersedes: the canonical event carries the final one and the provisional one stays on its supporting observation, never counted again.

1.caption: Full reasoning
1.description: The model's reasoning text as produced.

2.caption: Summary
2.description: A summary of the model's reasoning, not its full text.

3.caption: Redacted
3.description: The source reports that reasoning occurred but withholds its text (for example encrypted or redacted reasoning).

1.caption: Increment
1.description: The text continues the item's text: the item's text is the concatenation, in journal.sequence order, of the texts of its Increment blocks. An increment is not by itself asserted to be the whole text, and the assembled text is never concatenated with a whole text reported elsewhere (for example a turn's own response).

2.caption: Snapshot
2.description: The text is the item's whole text as of this record: it replaces any earlier view of the item and is never concatenated with one.

1.caption: Monetary amount
1.description: Money in the stated currency.

2.caption: Premium requests
2.description: A count of premium requests the CLI reports as consumed.

3.caption: Model cost multiplier
3.description: A per-call model multiplier, or a sum of such multipliers, that a vendor reports for billing; not money and not a request count.

4.caption: Nano-AIU
4.description: Nano AI units a vendor reports.

1.caption: Scope total
1.description: The consumption of exactly the observation's scope unit (for example one model response); observations of distinct units of that scope are disjoint.

2.caption: Cumulative snapshot
2.description: A running total of the scope unit from its start up to the point of observation. It may include consumption before this capture began and is not the unit's completed total; two snapshots of one unit overlap and are never summed.

3.caption: Single response
3.description: The consumption of one model response within the observation's scope unit, which the source may leave unidentified (for example the usage of a child run's last response that the spawning call's result reports): neither the unit's total nor a running total of it. It is never summed with the unit's other observations, and it is the same quantity as another observation only when both name the same response.

7.caption: Child run
7.description: The run of a sub-agent that a tool call spawned. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation); its observations are never added to the parent's or the run's totals.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A unit the source itself defines, which none of the other scopes describes; the sibling scope names it (for example Conversation step). It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation).

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source establishes this exact value as a measurement of the quantity; for a running total, of every contribution to it.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

3.caption: Conditional
3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.

5.caption: Conflicting

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded

applies_to.profiles: every reviewed assembly profile under ocsf/profiles/
applies_to.scope: the consolidated canonical events of a final assembly; every observation keeps the mapping contract of the source that produced it

embedded.executor: journal-ocsf-writer Assembler with AssemblyGate, AssemblyGrouping and EventMerge (direct Java over the observations the source mappers emitted)

rules.target: the class and activity of the consolidated observations
rules.meaning: one canonical event for one logical entity at one lifecycle stage that several sources observed: fields one source reports are taken from it, equal reports give their common value, number-spelling differences keep the primary's spelling, objects merge member by member and identified array elements element by element, and any other difference is a conflict left out of the canonical event and listed with every value

embedded.identity_layers: acquisition (journal.run_uid), source occurrence (artifact, record index, emit ordinal: assembly.occurrence_uid), logical entity and stage (assembly.entity_uid in a profile-declared namespace) and provider or protocol identity (tool_call_uid, response_uid, protocol objects) are distinct; a call id repeated across start, update and completion names stages of one entity, never a duplicate
embedded.gate: a source is part of the execution when the session identity its observations report, or its declared companion's, equals the run's (the first identity established in precedence order); another identity or several refuse it as another execution; a required source with none is refused as unestablished; the same acquisition origin with the same sha256 is the same import and is not imported again; identical bytes from distinct origins stay distinct sources
embedded.joins: observations relate only through the profile's declared joins: equal values at every key pointer, in the same core, directly or through a chain of joins across a third source; never by position, timestamp proximity or similar text; an identity repeated within one source from one mapping rule makes the entity ambiguous, and its observations stay canonical and flagged

merge.provenance_rule: each observation keeps its own; the consolidated event carries the primary's (the first in the profile's precedence)
merge.authority: a profile may declare, per class and field pointer, the source role whose value the canonical event carries when observations conflict, with its reason; the conflict stays listed with every value. Without a declaration no source wins and the field stays absent. Explicit mode whole-field selects the complete named field before structural union; every supporting field stays unchanged and the selection is independently checked. Omitted mode retains conflict-only semantics.
merge.finality: of usage observations of one quantity (same scope, aggregation and model), only those at the highest usage status reach the canonical event (Final over Provisional); the others are field evidence with relation 8 Superseded and stay on their supporting observations
merge.envelope: the consolidated event's class, activity, time, metadata, journal and source_ref are the primary observation's, or under a join that declares a stage order the most advanced stage's (a record the stream shows Partial and the session file Completed consolidates at Completed)
merge.copies: identical bytes accepted from distinct origins: the copies' observations of the same record and emit ordinal are one entity, so a copy never becomes extra executions
merge.own_rule: top-level members that belong to one observation (its assembly record and native residual data) are left out of the consolidated event and stay on each supporting observation; a nested data member is its object's native residual (provenance, the primary's kept) when that object states a basis or source_ref, and otherwise a fact that is compared
merge.partial_projections: partial MCP protocol projections of one protocol object (same definition and projection) merge member by member; the merged object's missing_required is the intersection of the projections' (a member one projection lacked and another supplied is complementary), and the merged object stays a partial projection, never a synthesized complete wire message

embedded.accounting: one canonical event per entity and stage carries one usage observation per scope, aggregation, finality and model, with every source that reported it in its field evidence, so overlapping reports of one quantity are never counted twice; different quantity kinds (money, premium requests, model cost multipliers, nano-AIU, credits) are separate observations and never compared or added; cumulative snapshots and per-call observations keep their own scopes and aggregations
embedded.order: each observation is written in precedence and arrival order (a canonical single observation, or a supporting observation) and each consolidated event right after its primary observation; journal.sequence is import order, never occurrence order

value.basis: codex.stream.thread_usage.v2: turn.completed carries ThreadTokenUsage.total, the thread's cumulative usage as of this turn's completion, including earlier turns of a resumed thread; not a per-turn measurement; final for this run; codex.stream.thread_usage_aggregation.v2: a running total of the thread up to this turn's completion that adds only the responses whose completion carried usage; never summed with another snapshot; codex.usage.component_measurement.v2: at rust-v0.160.1 the exec stream's usage is the thread running total (ThreadTokenUsage.total), the element-wise sum of the usage of each response whose completion carried one (TokenUsageInfo::append_last_usage); a completion without usage adds nothing (ResponseEvent::Completed.token_usage is an Option), and within a response an omitted cache_write_tokens, input_tokens_details or output_tokens_details is written as cache-write, cached or reasoning 0 (#[serde(default)], unwrap_or_default, unwrap_or(0)) while input_tokens and output_tokens are required. So no member establishes the thread's complete quantity, however large: with any non-zero member a zero cached, cache-write or reasoning member is Possibly default and every other member is a Lower bound (the thread's actual quantity is at least the member and may exceed it: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150); with every member zero (Usage::default, no update arrived) each is Possibly default
